title: Moody's Light: the lantern on the road near Rensselaer

sources.what: Light in an isolated field 'About 15 miles west of Francesville, in Rensselaer', shifting from 'bright yellow to a blood red'; one version: in the 'middle part of the last century' a family named Moody died in a house fire and the light is Old Man Moody searching for his family (the version adds that he hanged himself; left out); seen from Meridian Road, which 'would be 49 if the road went all the way through the cornfield'; the SouthLake chapter of the Indiana Ghost Trackers and the paper's reporters recreated the light from 49 ('this myth has been debunked', chapter director Chris Hensel); neighbor Anita Moore heard the legend 'as early as her teenage years, which would have been in the 1940's', 'I have seen the light that comes toward you' but 'I just always knew it was 49'; Granville 'Van' Moody, the last of the Moody line there, 'never had a family', quit farming in the 1930s and died in Francesville; the house stood empty from the early 1930s to the 1960s, and 'Some kids were out there one day fooling around and burned down the house'; light chasers knock on doors and get stuck in ditches.
sources.who: Rensselaer Republican, 'RIP: Local legend laid to rest' (staff report, Oct. 31, 2007)

sources.what: 'Legend has it that Old Man Moody came home late one night to find his house burning down, with his entire family dead inside. Moody's Light refers to Old Man Moody's orb searching for his lost family'; 'locals still swear that Moody's light is real.'
sources.who: Only In Your State, 'Here's The Ultimate Terrifying Indiana Road Trip'

sources.what: The murder version: farmer Moody came home to find his family killed; the light is his ghost 'searching the cornfield for his family's killer'; on a road between Rensselaer and Francesville.

Moody went out each night with a lantern 'searching for signs of the killer who took everything away from him and his family'; 'a local ghost-hunting group had claimed to debunk the story ... but others are not convinced'.
sources.who: Hauntings Around America, 'Moody's Light: Haunted Indiana'

sources.what: 'Moody's Light' is said to be the ghost of a farmer named Moody who carries a lantern while in search of the people who killed his family; on a gravel road called Moody Road.
Another version: Old Man Moody came home to his house burning with his family inside; the light was 'Moody's lantern, in search of someone', and seemed to get closer.
Saint Joseph's College students' version: Moody lost his family in a storm; to call him, face your car down the cornfield 'and flash your headlights three times.'
sources.who: Guilford Voyager, 'Halloween Horrors: Mr. Rush recalls "Moody's Light"' (2019)

sources.what: 'if you were to flash your car headlights three times, the light will appear and move slowly towards you'; someone who staked out the road blamed car headlights on a parallel road.
sources.who: Haunted Places of USA blog, 'The Moody Light - Francisville, Indiana' (2020)

sources.what: Student-collected Moody's Light accounts from Jasper County going back to 1971 (records 1666, Oct. 7, 1971; 930, 1971; 932, 1972; 938, 1986; 878, 1992; 1658, 1993; 1660, 1994; 1662, 2008); record 1852 describes lights around 'an abandoned mansion that was located on Van Moody road'.
sources.who: Indiana State University Folklore Archives, via the Indiana Digital Library

sources.what: State Road 49's southern end is at SR 14 in Barkley Township, 'about 10 miles northeast of Rensselaer'; it runs north from there.
sources.who: AARoads Wiki and Wikipedia, 'Indiana State Road 49'

sources.what: Moody is an unincorporated community in Jasper County, founded in 1893 by Granville Moody and named for him (Ronald L. Baker, From Needmore to Prosperity, IU Press, 1995, p. 226); its post office closed in 1923 (Blevins/Helbock list: open 1914, closed by 1923). Not used in the narration.

A Granville Moody's son Thomas (1884-1906) was killed by a falling tree (per the fact-check, citing Find a Grave), so the short makes no claim that the Moodys had no family tragedy, and drops the neighbor's 'never had a family' (Van may or may not have been the 1893 founder).
sources.who: Rensselaer Adventures blog, 'Tales from the graveyard 3' (Oct. 2019), as read by the fact-checker

sourcing_note: A legend, called a legend throughout. Its versions disagree (murder, a fire, a storm; one adds a hanging, left out under the series rules), so the short gives two versions as versions. Where it is: the Rensselaer Republican says Meridian Road, 'about 15 miles west of Francesville, in Rensselaer'; the ISU archive files it under Jasper County; one aggregator says Pulaski County, so the short says only 'near Rensselaer'. The 1940s memory, the last Moody's never having a family and the kids burning the empty house are one neighbor's words in one article, so they're attributed to her ('She said'). The headlight solution is the paper's and the Indiana Ghost Trackers' own 2007 investigation, attributed. Rensselaer's pronunciation is respelled 'Rensa-leer' (REN-suh-leer); unconfirmed with locals. Blind independent check Nov. 15: the headlight count varies (twice or three times), so 'three times' came out; 'never had a family' came out (a Granville Moody founded Moody in 1893 and lost a son in 1906, and nothing shows whether Van was that man), replaced by the paper's own 'quit farming in the 1930s'; the article never says 'headlights', only that the team 'recreated Moody's Light from 49', so the narration says that; the murder version gets a dark house and only the fire version shows fire (split into two beats, and the neighbor's two lines joined into one beat to stay at eight); the label reads 2007 (the article's date, not the night of the hunt).

beats.text: Out in the fields near Rensselaer, Indiana, people say a lantern comes toward you in the dark.
beats.label: NEAR RENSSELAER, INDIANA
beats.credit: Rensselaer Republican, Oct. 31, 2007; Only In Your State

beats.text: The legend says it's Old Man Moody, still searching for his family.
beats.label: THE LEGEND
beats.credit: Rensselaer Republican, 2007; Only In Your State

beats.text: In one version, they were murdered.
beats.label: ONE VERSION
beats.credit: Hauntings Around America; Esoteric Synaptic Events (2013)

beats.text: In another, they died when his house burned.
beats.label: ANOTHER VERSION
beats.credit: Rensselaer Republican, Oct. 31, 2007; Only In Your State

beats.text: To call him, the story goes, you flash your headlights.
beats.credit: Haunted Places of USA; Nicole Mathew (2023); ObscUrban Legend

beats.text: A neighbor told the Rensselaer Republican she'd heard the legend as a teenager, in the 1940s. The paper said the last Moody there, Van Moody, quit farming in the 1930s, and she said kids later burned his empty house.
beats.label: RENSSELAER REPUBLICAN
beats.credit: Rensselaer Republican, Oct. 31, 2007; ISU Folklore Archives

beats.text: In 2007, ghost hunters and the paper said they'd solved it: they recreated the light from State Road 49. Not everyone believes them.
beats.credit: Rensselaer Republican, 2007; Wikipedia; Only In Your State

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
